title: Procurement security question bank for evaluation committees
content:
Purpose and audience
This is a lightweight question bank and response playbook intended for sales, CSEs, and procurement-facing reps supporting customer evaluation committees (security, risk, legal, procurement). Use it during RFPs, security reviews, and contract negotiations to: (1) anticipate common gating questions, (2) provide consistent, auditable answers, and (3) accelerate procurement cycles.

How to use this doc
- Pick the categories relevant to the buyer (SOC2/ISO/HIPAA).
- Provide the short answer in a one-liner for execs, then the longer technical detail for security reviewers.
- Mark items that require legal/engineering escalation with [ESCL].
- Use the redline snippets under "Suggested audit-log clause" when negotiating contract language.

Top-level one-liners (for quick replies)
- SOC 2 status: Redwood Inference maintains a SOC 2 Type II program with annual audits; we can provide certified report under NDA.
- ISO 27001: We maintain controls aligned to ISO 27001; formal certification (customer-specific) available via dedicated contracts for enterprise/private deployments.
- HIPAA: We support HIPAA workloads via our Private offering (VPC/on-prem + BAA). We do not ingest PHI in shared-hosted default plans.
- Audit logs: Customer-level audit logs (auth, admin, API usage, model selection) are retained per contract; custom retention windows available as an add-on.

Common procurement questions and model answers (organized by theme)
1) Compliance and certification
Q: Do you have SOC 2 Type II? Can we get the report?
A-short: Yes — SOC 2 Type II; report available under NDA.
A-long: We run a mature SOC 2 Type II program covering infrastructure, change management, access control, and incident response. We rotate auditors annually and can provide the most recent report under a standard NDA. For higher-assurance customers we map control sets to customer requirements in a controls matrix (deliverable). [ESCL]

Q: Are you ISO 27001 certified?
A-short: Controls mapped; certification options for enterprise/private customers.
A-long: Our internal control set is aligned to ISO 27001 and we maintain documented ISMS processes. We currently pursue formal certification for designated private/dedicated customer programs; contact AE for the certification track and timeline.

2) HIPAA and data handling
Q: Can you sign a BAA and host PHI?
A-short: Yes — via Redwood Private or Dedicated with a BAA. Not in our shared-hosted free-tier.
A-long: We will only accept PHI on Private/Dedicated contracts that include a BAA. Our Private deployment options allow for customer-controlled keys, private networking (VPC), and audit log streams shipped to customer telemetry. For hosted API customers, we recommend pseudonymization and tokenization patterns; we do not recommend sending unencrypted PHI to the shared tenant. [ESCL]

Q: How do you delete customer data and what is the retention model?
A-short: Data retention configurable per contract; default retention windows and deletion APIs documented.
A-long: Requests to delete data are executed per contract SLA. For hosted tiers we maintain short default retention for request payloads and logs; for Dedicated/Private customers the control plane exposes retention windows and deletion endpoints. Deletion is logical and physical lifecycle actions are tracked in audit logs. When required, we provide a data destruction certificate for on-prem or dedicated workloads.

3) Auditability and logging
Q: What audit logs are available and what do they contain?
A-short: Auth events, admin changes, API request metadata, model variant served, billing events.
A-long: Audit logs include time-stamped records for: authentication and authorization events (login, token issuance, key rotation), administrative actions (role changes, policy updates), API request metadata (request id, path, model id, sequence length, tokens billed), model variant and runtime (quantization/variant used), and billing/usage records. Logs can be exported to customer SIEMs via secure syslog/S3 connectors and streamed in near-real time for Private/Dedicated customers.

Q: Can logs be tamper-evident?
A-short: Yes — options for append-only, signed log exports and customer-side ingestion.
A-long: For high-assurance customers we offer signed log export (SHA-256) and timestamping to support tamper-evidence. Our architecture can also route logs to a customer-managed destination (S3 with object locking or an on-prem SIEM) where immutability controls can be applied. [ESCL]

4) Access controls and identity
Q: How granular are RBAC and key controls?
A-short: Role-based access controls with API keys, scoped tokens, and org/team level roles.
A-long: We support org, team, and token-level scoping. Admin roles are segregated from runtime roles; keys can be scoped to a given model, route, or environment. For Dedicated/Private we support customer-managed KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, HSM) and rotation policies.

5) Operational security & incident response
Q: What is your incident response SLA and notification process?
A-short: Tiered incident categorization and customer notification commitments included in enterprise SLA.
A-long: Incidents are classified by severity. For Sev-1 incidents affecting availability or data exposure, we notify customers within the contractual window and publish a post-incident report. We maintain a runbook, tabletop exercise cadence, and contact roster for account-level escalation.

Negotiation flags (what to watch for and escalate)
- Don’t commit to on-the-spot certifications or custom attestations without legal signoff.
- Avoid broad data residency promises for hosted tenants; prefer Private/Dedicated for strict residency requirements.
- Escalate requests for raw model logits/parameters or training data access (rare; requires research/legal review).
- For long-term retention or immutability demands requiring system changes, flag as engineering scope and schedule impact.

Suggested audit-log clause (quick redline snippet for contracts)
"Provider shall generate and retain audit records documenting Authentication events, Administrative changes, API requests (including request ID and model variant), and Billing events for the Customer's tenant(s). Audit records shall be made available to Customer via secure export (S3, syslog, or direct SIEM integration) and retained for a period defined in the Order Form. For Dedicated/Private customers, Provider will support customer-configured export and immutability settings (e.g., S3 Object Lock). Provider will provide a tamper-evidence summary upon reasonable request."

Quick rebuttal templates for common procurement pushes
- Customer: "We need PHI processing on your hosted plan."
  Sales: "We recommend Private with a BAA for PHI. Our hosted tier limits on-host PHI intake for security and compliance reasons — we can map a migration path and timeline in the contract."
- Customer: "We require ISO certification immediately."
  Sales: "Our controls are aligned and we can provide a controls mapping now; formal certification for a dedicated program is available on an enterprise track — let's start the certification SLA conversation."

Operational handoffs (what to include when escalating to AE/CSE/legal/eng)
- Attach the customer's prioritized security questions and label each with: priority (P0/P1/P2), who asked it (contact + role), the desired answer format (report, diagram, redline), and whether they require NDA/BAA.
- Tag items requiring engineering changes (e.g., longer retention, signed logs) with expected lead time and rough cost estimate.
- Provide copies of prior customer redlines and negotiation history if available.

Appendix: evidence checklist for fast turnaround
- Most-requested items: latest SOC 2 Type II report (NDA), controls matrix mapping to ISO 27001, BAA template, sample audit-log export (schema), network architecture diagram for Private offering, key rotation policy, incident response playbook excerpts.
